title: Adaptive kernel-selection telemetry harness and staged CI perf gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current CI perf gates rely on a small set of static golden baselines and synthetic workloads that do not capture interactions between kernel selection, attention path variants (flash/standard/sparse), and prefill vs decode scheduling modes. This leads to flaky latency regressions when we land runtime or kernel changes.

Goal: Build a telemetry-driven harness that can: 1) collect representative kernel/attention usage from production traces, 2) synthesize a small, deterministic multi-workload suite that exercises kernel routing and prefill/decode scheduling hotspots, and 3) add staged CI gates (smoke -> candidate -> blocking) with clear latency/throughput SLO checks and actionable failure artifacts.

Success metrics: sustained CI false-positive rate < 2% on perf gates, end-to-end regression triage time < 4 hours for a perf failure, and coverage of top-10 kernel/attention permutations from production traces in the golden suite.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness binary or runner that replays synthesized workload traces with controllable seed and environment flags
A telemetry ingestion job that maps live requests to kernel-selection + attention-variant histograms (at daily granularity)
An initial golden suite of 12 deterministic scenarios covering top kernel/attention/prefill-decode permutations, checked into repo with manifests
Three-stage CI gating implemented: smoke (quick), candidate (longer, non-blocking), blocking (nightly blocking regression) with thresholded SLO checks
Failure artifacts: per-scenario latency P50/P95/P99 dumps, kernel routing decision logs, and a linkable perf-diff artifact that triagers can open
notes: We will prioritize scenarios that combine long prefill + short decode (chat-like) and short prefill + long decode (completion-heavy), since they exercise different KV cache and kernel reuse patterns.

Trade-off: full stochastic replay of production traces is expensive and non-deterministic. We will instead derive deterministic seeds from sampled traces and store synthetic seeds as the golden baseline.
Consider adding a lightweight quantization-aware scenario to catch regressions when kernel selection favors quantized paths.
Will coordinate with infra to pin GPU types in the CI candidate stage to reduce variance (NVIDIA A800 vs A100 noise observed previously).
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket opened. Collected stakeholder list: runtime, kernel-team, perf infra, QA. Suggested scope: telemetry -> synth suite -> staged CI. Requesting 8 points.

2026-02-16 Liam Chen: PoC telemetry job landed in infra-telemetry (PR: github.com/redwood/infra-telemetry/pull/224). Job extracts per-request kernel routing tags and attention-variant tags. Sampling set to 1% to start.
2026-02-20 Performance notes: early traces show top 6 kernel/attention permutations account for 78% of tail latency regressions in the last 30d window.
2026-02-25 Design review (runtime working group): decided to keep the golden seeds in the repo under /bench/goldens and to add a seeded-mode flag to the harness runner for deterministic runs.
2026-03-02 PR opened for harness runner skeleton: github.com/redwood/runtime-bench/pull/89. Uses deterministic RNG + synthetic token distributions derived from sampled traces.
2026-03-04 QA feedback (Morgan Reyes): Candidate runs show 7% variance in P95 across identical seeds on A100; infra suggested pinning environment and disabling hyperthreading for CI candidate stage.

2026-03-06 Kernel-team review (Dr. Elena Gomez): Requested additional instrumentation to log kernel-selection confidence scores to help root-cause when the runtime chooses slower kernels after a change.
2026-03-08 Liam Chen: Implemented per-scenario artifact upload to perf-dash (internal dashboard). Artifacts include timeline of kernel choices, decoded token counts, and KV hit/miss rates.

2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Moving to In Progress. Next steps: finalize golden manifest (12 scenarios), add smoke CI job (5 min budget), and draft blocking nightly job with 24-hour cadence. Assigned to Liam for implementation and to Morgan for QA test plans.
